statements.text: SAV1 carried mutations in 2.9% of 672 intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma samples, that is 20 samples.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We find that SAV1 was mutated in 2.9% (20/672) of 672 ICC samples.
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly this mutation rate for SAV1 across 672 ICC samples.

statements.text: Aristolochic acid exposure was more common than aflatoxin exposure among the Chinese ICC patients studied.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We identify six mutational signatures, including Signatures A and F, which are highly similar to previously described signatures linked to aristolochic acid and aflatoxin exposures, respectively.
statements.note: Both signatures are reported as resembling known exposure signatures, but how often each occurs is never compared.

statements.text: Tumors carrying SAV1 mutations had higher SAV1 protein levels and longer overall survival than tumors without them.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: SAV1 mutation is associated with lower SAV1 protein levels, higher rates of tumor recurrence, and shorter overall patient survival.
statements.note: The abstract reports the opposite: SAV1 mutation went with lower protein levels and shorter survival.

statements.text: Inactivating SAV1 shut down Hippo signaling, which activated YAP and drove tumor growth and metastasis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: its inactivation suppresses Hippo signaling, leading to YAP activation, thereby promoting tumor growth and metastasis
statements.note: This is the mechanism the biofunctional experiments report for loss of SAV1.

statements.text: The repressive and the activating ZFP189 factors shifted transposable element expression in the prefrontal cortex in the same direction.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: have opposite influence on the expression of genetic transposable elements
statements.note: RNA sequencing showed the two factors of opposing regulatory function had opposite effects on transposable element expression.

statements.text: ZFP189-driven transcription pushed transduced pyramidal neurons toward mature dendritic spine morphology.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ZFP189-mediated transcriptional control promotes mature dendritic spine morphology on transduced pyramidal neurons
statements.note: This is the structural effect reported after viral delivery of the synthetic factors.

statements.text: Delivering the activating ZFP189 factor increased the number of new transposable element insertions in prefrontal cortex neurons.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: RNA sequencing of virally manipulated prefrontal cortex tissues reveals that ZFP189 transcription factors of opposing regulatory function (ZFP189 WT versus ZFP189 VPR ) have opposite influence on the expression of genetic transposable elements
statements.note: Only transposable element transcript levels were measured; no new genomic insertions were assayed.

statements.text: Inverting ZFP189-mediated transcription in prefrontal cortex produced deficits in social interaction, motivation and social hierarchy cognition, with no other behavioral deficits seen.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: precipitates social behavioral deficits in terms of social interaction, motivation, and the cognition necessary for the maintenance of social hierarchy, without other observable behavioral deficits
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly these three social deficits and no others.

statements.text: Across 110 needle uses by eight surgeons, no ocular complications such as hyphema, wound leak or hypotony occurred.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A total of 110 needle uses by eight surgeons were included. No ocular complications occurred, including lens or iris injury, hyphema, AC collapse, wound leak, hypotony, infection, or retinal complication
statements.note: The primary outcome was zero ocular complications over all 110 uses.

statements.text: Two uses, 1.8% of the total, involved partial-thickness entry that never reached the anterior chamber, without damage to the eye.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Two technical events without ocular sequelae were noted, in which needle entry was partial thickness and did not reach the AC (1.8%; exact 95% CI, 0.2%–6.4%).
statements.note: These were the only technical events, reported at a rate of 1.8% with no ocular sequelae.

statements.text: Aqueous humor collected with the 32-gauge needle yielded more DNA for molecular analysis than aqueous humor taken with a 30-gauge needle.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Physicians rated needle entry, handling, and sample recovery as good or excellent.
statements.note: Sample recovery was rated subjectively by the surgeons; no molecular yield was measured or compared.

statements.text: Only a minority of the surgeons preferred the 32-gauge needle over the 30-gauge needle for future anterior chamber taps.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: All surgeons rated it better or much better for intra-procedural safety and preferred it for future AC taps.
statements.note: Every surgeon, not a minority, preferred the study needle for future taps.

statements.text: Treating ATRX-deficient sarcoma patients with epigenetic drugs improved their survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Future clinical trials investigating epigenetic therapies could offer novel treatment strategies for ATRX-deficient sarcomas.
statements.note: Epigenetic therapy is raised only as future work; no patient was treated in this study.

statements.text: Among transposable elements differentially expressed with ATRX loss, 97%, that is 93 elements, were upregulated.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ATRX loss was associated with loss of TE silencing with 97% (n=93) of differentially expressed TEs upregulated
statements.note: The abstract gives exactly this fraction of upregulated transposable elements.

statements.text: The 269 differentially methylated CpGs showed a marked hypermethylation effect with ATRX loss.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Methylation profiling identified 269 differentially methylated CpGs (FDR<0.05), with a marked hypomethylation effect.
statements.note: The direction is reversed: the reported effect is marked hypomethylation.

statements.text: In leiomyosarcoma, median overall survival was 81.0 months with ATRX retained against 34.9 months with ATRX lost.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The median overall survival in LMS patients was 81.0 vs 34.9 months for tumors with ATRX retention and loss (p log-rank =0.0023).
statements.note: These are the two median survival figures reported for LMS by ATRX status.

statements.text: Methyltransferase-like 3 deficiency drove naive human embryonic stem cells into a totipotent-like state and reactivated ERV1 and ERVL-MaLR elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: methyltransferase-like 3 deficiency reverts naive human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) to a totipotent-like state with reactivation and chromatin resetting of 8C-associated genes, eRNAs, and LTRs, particularly ERV1 and ERVL-MaLR
statements.note: This is the central result reported for loss of methyltransferase-like 3.

statements.text: Humans and mice use the same LINE-1 subfamilies, not species-specific ones, to regulate LTR activity through m6A.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: humans and mice employ species-specific long interspersed nuclear element-1 subfamilies with m 6 A to regulate LTR activity
statements.note: The abstract states the LINE-1 subfamilies involved are species-specific.

statements.text: In naive hESCs, m6A on L1PA blocked EP300 binding at ERV1 and strengthened KAP1 binding at ERVL-MaLR, restricting LTR activity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: m 6 A on L1PA suppresses EP300 binding to ERV1 and enhances KAP1 binding to ERVL-MaLR, thereby restricting LTR activity
statements.note: This is the binding mechanism the abstract describes in naive hESCs.

statements.text: Methyltransferase-like 3 deficiency slowed the proliferation of naive human embryonic stem cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We demonstrate that methyltransferase-like 3 deficiency reverts naive human embryonic stem cells (hESCs) to a totipotent-like state with reactivation and chromatin resetting of 8C-associated genes, eRNAs, and LTRs, particularly ERV1 and ERVL-MaLR
statements.note: The abstract reports a change of cell state and chromatin but no growth or proliferation measurement.

statements.text: Blood is the least readily available of the tissues from which cell-free DNA can be extracted.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: CtDNA is a fraction of circulating free DNA (cfDNA) that can be extracted from various tissues, with blood being the most readily available.
statements.note: The abstract calls blood the most readily available source, not the least.

statements.text: Streck tubes are the recommended blood collection tubes for maximizing the yield of plasma separation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: To maximize the yield of plasma separation, specific Streck tubes are recommended for blood collection.
statements.note: The abstract recommends these tubes for exactly this purpose.

statements.text: The sequencing approach calls somatic variants at a variant allele frequency of 5% or higher that are absent from the germline lineage.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: enabling the identification of somatic variants with a Variant Allele Frequency (VAF) of 5 % or higher, which are absent in the germline lineage
statements.note: This is the stated variant allele frequency threshold for somatic calls.

statements.text: The MagPurix kit recovers more cfDNA from plasma than column-based extraction kits.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The MagPurix CFC DNA Extraction Kit can be used for cfDNA extraction, and the TWIST Library Preparation protocol can be optimized for further analysis.
statements.note: The kit is named as usable for extraction but is never benchmarked against another method.

statements.text: At 10 micrograms per millilitre, the Mn3O4 nanozyme raised IL-10 secretion 8.3-fold while lowering TNF-alpha, IL-6 and IL-1beta.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In vitro, 10 μg/mL Mn 3 O 4 was cytocompatible, protected BMSCs and chondrocytes from H 2 O 2 -induced apoptosis, and reshaped inflammatory secretion, with IL-10 increased 8.3-fold and TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-1β reduced.
statements.note: The abstract gives this concentration and the 8.3-fold IL-10 increase with reduction of the three cytokines.

statements.text: MNKB/HA reduced pain behaviour in the rat osteoarthritis model.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: In rat OA, intra-articular MNKB/HA reduced OARSI scores, restored COL II and ACAN, decreased MMP13, improved subchondral bone microarchitecture, and attenuated synovitis and osteophytes.
statements.note: The rat outcomes are histological, structural and molecular; no pain or gait measure is reported.

statements.text: In rat joints the hydrogel stayed intra-articular for at least ten days with no notable systemic toxicity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: showed intra-articular retention for at least 10 days without notable systemic toxicity
statements.note: Retention of at least ten days without notable systemic toxicity is stated directly.

statements.text: In rat osteoarthritis, MNKB/HA raised synovial cfDNA levels and pushed macrophages toward M1 polarization.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: MNKB/HA also reduced synovial cfDNA, weakened TLR9 signaling, promoted M2 polarization
statements.note: The abstract reports reduced synovial cfDNA and promotion of M2, not M1, polarization.

statements.text: Captafol mainly increased C to A substitutions, whereas malathion produced mostly C to T substitutions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: captafol increased C to A mutations primarily, while malathion induced mostly C to T mutations
statements.note: These are the two compound-specific base substitution patterns reported.

statements.text: Malathion induced H2A.X phosphorylation and G2/M cell cycle arrest alongside its mutagenic effect.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: malathion did not induce DNA damage markers or cell cycle alterations despite its mutagenic effect
statements.note: Malathion induced neither DNA damage markers nor cell cycle alterations; those belonged to captafol.

statements.text: Of the six pesticides tested, only captafol at 200 nM and malathion at 100 micromolar were clearly mutagenic in TK6 cells.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Whole genome sequencing of TK6 human lymphoblastoid cell clones following 30-day exposure at subtoxic concentrations revealed a clear mutagenic effect of treatment with captafol or malathion when added at 200 nM or 100 μM initial concentrations, respectively.
statements.note: Only these two compounds were mutagenic, at exactly these initial concentrations.

statements.text: Exposing cells to captafol and malathion together produced more mutations than either compound alone.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Each pesticide induced a specific base substitution mutational signature: captafol increased C to A mutations primarily, while malathion induced mostly C to T mutations.
statements.note: Each pesticide was tested on its own; no combined exposure arm is described.

statements.text: Plasma cfDNA concentration on its own separated patients with active HCC from control patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: All samples were analysed for cell free DNA (cfDNA) concentration, and for mutations in TERT promoter, CTNNB1 , TP53 , PIK3CA and NFE2L2 by sequencing and droplet-based digital PCR.
statements.note: cfDNA concentration was measured in every sample, but the abstract reports no result for it.

statements.text: The ctDNA mutation rate fell as tumour stage became more advanced.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: CtDNA mutation rate increased with advanced tumour stages
statements.note: The direction is reversed: the mutation rate increased with advanced stage.

statements.text: Mutated ctDNA was found in 40.2% of active HCC patients, 14.6% of inactive HCC patients and 1.8% of controls.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In patients with active HCC, 40.2% of the ctDNA was mutated vs 14.6% in patients with inactive HCC and 1.8% in controls
statements.note: These are the three mutation rates reported across the groups.

statements.text: The study analysed 772 plasma samples from 173 HCC patients plus 56 plasmas from chronic liver disease patients without HCC.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We analysed 772 plasmas from 173 patients with HCC collected at the time of diagnosis or treatment (n=502), 24 hours after locoregional treatment (n=154) and during follow-up (n=116). For controls, 56 plasmas from patients with chronic liver disease without HCC were analysed.
statements.note: These sample and patient counts are stated in the design.

statements.text: Functional assays of UV-induced 6-4 photoproducts showed ccRCC cells to be proficient in nucleotide excision repair.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Functional assays showed NER deficiency in ccRCC cells.
statements.note: The functional assays showed deficiency, not proficiency.

statements.text: Irofulven sensitivity rose in some ccRCC cell lines, and PTGR1, which activates irofulven, tracked with that sensitivity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Irofulven sensitivity increased in some cell lines. Prostaglandin reductase 1 (PTGR1), which activates irofulven, was also associated with this sensitivity.
statements.note: Both the partial sensitivity increase and the PTGR1 association are reported results.

statements.text: ccRCC patients given irofulven survived longer than patients receiving standard care.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These patients may be responsive to irofulven, a previously abandoned anticancer agent that has minimal activity in NER-proficient cells.
statements.note: Responsiveness is predicted from cell lines and mutational signatures; no patients were treated.

statements.text: About 10% of ccRCC patients in TCGA carried the NER deficiency signature together with substantial PTGR1 expression.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Approximately 10% of ccRCC patients in the TCGA cohort showed mutational signatures consistent with ERCC2 inactivation associated NER deficiency and also substantial levels of PTGR1 expression.
statements.note: This is the fraction of the TCGA cohort the abstract estimates.

statements.text: The 2 Mb panel covers 15,000 genome-wide SNPs, 500 focal SNPs in driver regions and exons of 81 commonly altered genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: It includes 15,000 genome-wide SNPs, 500 focal SNPs in breast cancer driver regions, and exons from 81 commonly altered genes
statements.note: These are exactly the panel contents listed.

statements.text: eSENSES detected copy number alterations in matched tumour tissue as reliably as in blood.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: To enhance the detection of somatic copy number alterations (SCNAs) and circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA), we developed eSENSES, a 2 Mb breast cancer-targeted NGS panel.
statements.note: Performance was assessed on synthetic and clinical samples with no comparison against tumour tissue.

statements.text: In metastatic breast cancer patients, eSENSES ctDNA estimates showed no relation to disease progression.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In patients with metastatic breast cancer, ctDNA estimations correlated with disease progression.
statements.note: The abstract reports that the ctDNA estimations did correlate with progression.

statements.text: eSENSES detected ctDNA fractions below 1% and was highly sensitive and specific at 2-3% ctDNA levels.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: eSENSES can detect ctDNA levels below 1%, exhibiting high sensitivity and specificity at 2-3% ctDNA levels
statements.note: Both the sub-1% detection and the 2-3% performance claim are stated.

statements.text: Correcting GC bias with GCfix improved cancer detection accuracy from cfDNA fragmentomic classifiers.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: However, cfDNA fragmentomics and copy number analysis can be complicated by GC bias.
statements.note: GC bias is given as a complication for fragmentomics, but no downstream diagnostic result is reported.

statements.text: GCfix works with any reference genome and outputs correction factors, tagged BAM files and corrected coverage tracks.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: It works on all reference genomes and generates correction factors, tagged BAM files, and corrected coverage tracks.
statements.note: These are exactly the stated capabilities and outputs.

statements.text: GCfix corrects GC bias only in high-coverage cfDNA data.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We present GCfix, a method for robust GC bias correction in cfDNA data across diverse coverages.
statements.note: GCfix is presented as robust across diverse coverage levels, not restricted to high coverage.

statements.text: On the two new performance metrics introduced in the paper, GCfix beat existing cfDNA GC bias correction methods.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: GCfix outperforms existing cfDNA GC bias correction methods on these metrics.
statements.note: The abstract states GCfix outperformed existing methods on the two metrics introduced.

statements.text: Peaks of roughly 28 nt piRNAs coincided with reduced expression of horizontally transferred and resident transposons, mainly during embryogenesis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: peak levels of ∼28 nt long piRNAs correlate with reduced HTT and resident TE expression primarily during embryogenesis
statements.note: This correlation, with that piRNA length and developmental window, is the reported result.

statements.text: The siRNA pathway, and not the piRNA pathway, responded to the horizontally transferred transposons in Rhodnius prolixus.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: reveal that piRNAs, but not the siRNA pathway, responded to HTTs that were recently transferred from vertebrate tetrapods to a hematophagous insect of medical relevance
statements.note: The pathways are swapped: piRNAs responded, the siRNA pathway did not.

statements.text: Resident transposon piRNAs showed typical ping-pong signatures, while sense and antisense HTT piRNAs overlapped by about 20 nt or showed none.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: while resident TEs piRNAs seem to engage in a typical ping-pong amplification mechanism, sense and antisense HTT piRNAs instead overlap by ∼20 nt or do not display ping-pong signatures
statements.note: This contrast between resident and horizontally transferred element piRNAs is reported directly.

statements.text: Knocking down Rp-PIWI genes increased transposon expression in Rhodnius prolixus.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: RNA-Seq data was used to quantify transposon and Rp-PIWI genes expression levels and were validated by qRT-PCR.
statements.note: Rp-PIWI expression was only quantified; no knockdown experiment is described.

statements.text: Silencing HSPA5 increased glioma cell proliferation, migration and invasion.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Silencing HSPA5 expression may lead to the inhibition of glioma cell proliferation, migration, invasion and resistance to apoptosis.
statements.note: Silencing HSPA5 is reported to inhibit, not increase, these processes.

statements.text: The heat shock protein gene signature predicted glioma response to temozolomide.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Additionally, we developed a nomogram incorporating clinical parameters and the HSPGs signature to enhance prognostic prediction.
statements.note: The signature and nomogram are built for prognosis; no treatment response analysis is reported.

statements.text: A signature of four heat shock protein-associated genes was an independent prognostic factor for glioma in TCGA and CGGA data.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we identified a signature of 4 HSPGs as an independent prognostic factor for glioma
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this four-gene independent prognostic signature.

statements.text: Higher risk scores from the model went together with a more immunosuppressive state in glioma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Immunoenrichment analysis revealed a correlation between the risk score and the immunosuppressive status of glioma.
statements.note: The immunoenrichment analysis reported this correlation.

statements.text: MUC5B mutations appeared in 7.7% of precancerous lesions and 6.7% of esophageal squamous cell carcinomas.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Mutations in MUC5B were observed in 7.7% of precancerous lesions and 6.7% of ESCC.
statements.note: These are the two MUC5B mutation frequencies reported.

statements.text: APOBEC-associated mutational signatures were found only in the carcinomas, not in squamous dysplasia.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Apolipoprotein B mRNA-editing catalytic polypeptide-like (APOBEC) enzyme-associated mutational signatures were exclusively identified in ESCC
statements.note: The abstract states these signatures were exclusive to the carcinoma samples.

statements.text: Copy number alterations were more frequent than structural variants in esophageal squamous dysplasia.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our results revealed frequent copy number alterations (CNAs) and structural variants (SVs) in esophageal squamous dysplasia.
statements.note: Both classes are called frequent in dysplasia, but their relative frequency is never compared.

statements.text: Dysplasia that recurred locally within two years had lower ploidy alteration levels than dysplasia without long-term recurrence.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the cohort that underwent local recurrence of dysplasia within two years had significantly elevated ploidy alterations levels compared to those with no long-term recurrence
statements.note: The recurrence cohort had significantly elevated, not lower, ploidy alterations.

statements.text: The 13 satellite DNA families are concentrated at the centromeres of the six chromosomes.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The satellitome analysis discovered 13 satellite DNA families that comprise about 0.15% of the entire genome.
statements.note: Their number and genome fraction are given, but nothing is said about where they sit on chromosomes.

statements.text: The 1.67 Gb genome holds 731.63 Mb of repetitive sequence, with Class II elements making up 443.25 Mb.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The results indicated that the genome was 1.67 Gb, with 731.63 Mb of repetitive sequences, comprising 27% of Class II (443.25 Mb), 16% of Class I (268.45 Mb), and 1% of unknown TEs (19.92 Mb).
statements.note: These genome and repeat sizes are reported exactly.

statements.text: Chromosome size and repetitive sequence content correlated almost perfectly, with a Pearson r of 0.99.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a significant linear correlation (Pearson correlation: r = 0.99, p-value = 0.00003) between the size of the chromosomes and the repetitive sequences
statements.note: The abstract gives this correlation coefficient for chromosome size against repeat content.

statements.text: Retrotransposons were transcriptionally more active than DNA transposons in Xya riparia.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the transcriptional analysis of TEs found that DNA transposons were more transcriptionally active than retrotransposons
statements.note: The transcriptional analysis found the reverse, with DNA transposons more active.

statements.text: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio was significantly associated with ctDNA detection, with an odds ratio of 4.01.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (OR = 4.01 [1.85; 8.71]) were significantly associated with ctDNA detection
statements.note: This odds ratio for the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio is reported directly.

statements.text: The biochemical parameters evaluated were significantly associated with pathological downstaging and recurrence.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Associations between biochemical parameters and pathological downstaging or recurrence were not observed.
statements.note: No such associations were observed for either outcome.

statements.text: Kidney and liver function markers showed no significant association with plasma ctDNA detection in muscle-invasive bladder cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Significant associations between kidney or liver function markers and ctDNA detection were not observed.
statements.note: This null result for organ function markers is the study's main finding.

statements.text: Patients with detectable ctDNA had shorter overall survival than ctDNA-negative patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Elevated leukocyte-based immune markers were observed in ctDNA-positive patients, but the evaluated biochemical parameters showed no prognostic value.
statements.note: Prognostic value is reported for the biochemical markers only; survival by ctDNA status is never given.

statements.text: Patients with TMB-high tumours had significantly shorter overall survival than TMB-low patients.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with TMB-high tumors showed significantly shorter RFS compared to the TMB-low group (median 24.2 vs. 37.1 months; p = 0.008), whereas OS was not significantly different.
statements.note: Relapse-free survival was shorter in TMB-high tumours, but overall survival did not differ significantly.

statements.text: Median relapse-free survival was 24.2 months for TMB-high tumours against 37.1 months for TMB-low tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients with TMB-high tumors showed significantly shorter RFS compared to the TMB-low group (median 24.2 vs. 37.1 months; p = 0.008)
statements.note: These are the two reported median relapse-free survival times.

statements.text: Among patients without recurrence in the first two years, TMB-high was the only independent factor for late recurrence, hazard ratio 2.45.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In the subgroup without early recurrence, TMB-high status was the only independent factor associated with late recurrence (HR, 2.45; p = 0.005).
statements.note: The subgroup analysis reports exactly this hazard ratio and exclusivity.

statements.text: TMB-high tumours were larger at resection than TMB-low tumours.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: TMB-high tumors correlated with advanced liver fibrosis and specific somatic mutations (CTNNB1, TTN, MUC16).
statements.note: The reported correlates are fibrosis and specific mutations; tumour size is never mentioned.

statements.text: Across 10,257 tumours from 34 cancer types the analysis identified 52,277 cancer-specific transposon fusion transcripts.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: performed a pan-cancer analysis of 10,257 cancer samples across 34 cancer types as well as 3,088 normal tissue samples. We identified 52,277 cancer-specific fusions
statements.note: These cohort sizes and the fusion count are stated directly.

statements.text: Tumours carrying more transposon fusions responded better to immune checkpoint blockade.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We also demonstrated that transposon-derived peptides triggered CD8+ T-cell activation to the extent comparable to EBV viruses.
statements.note: T-cell activation was measured directly, but no immunotherapy outcome is reported.

statements.text: Alu source elements, like L1s and HERVs, lost DNA methylation in cancer when fusions formed.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Source L1s and HERVs, but not Alus showed decreased DNA methylation in cancer upon fusion formation.
statements.note: Decreased methylation applied to source L1s and HERVs but explicitly not to Alus.

statements.text: Cancer-specific L1 fusions were enriched in tumour suppressors while Alu fusions were enriched in oncogenes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Overall cancer-specific L1 fusions were enriched in tumor suppressors while Alu fusions were enriched in oncogenes
statements.note: This split between L1 and Alu fusion targets is reported directly.

statements.text: The classifier separated stage 0 from stage 2 breast cancers.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Here, we conducted a case-control study to develop a plasma-based protein classifier to distinguish between early-stage breast cancer patients and healthy individuals.
statements.note: The classifier was built to tell early-stage cancer from healthy controls; no within-stage discrimination is reported.

statements.text: The study compared 219 treatment-naive breast cancer patients against 116 healthy controls.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: A total of 335 women, comprising 116 patients with newly diagnosed, treatment naïve breast cancer (Stage 0-2) and 219 healthy controls
statements.note: The group sizes are swapped: 116 patients and 219 healthy controls.

statements.text: Under leave-one-out cross-validation the classifier reached an AUC of 0.96, with 86.2% sensitivity and 90.4% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The classifier achieved an AUC of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.93-0.97), with a sensitivity of 86.2% (95% CI: 78.8-91.3%) and a specificity of 90.4% (95% CI: 85.8-93.6%).
statements.note: These are the headline performance figures reported.

statements.text: Sensitivity stayed above 85% in both low-density (87.2%) and high-density (90.2%) breasts at 90% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the classifier retained >85% sensitivity regardless of breast density (low density: 87.2%, high density: 90.2%) at 90% specificity
statements.note: Both density-specific sensitivities are given at fixed 90% specificity.

statements.text: LinG3D is distributed as open-source routines written in MATLAB, Python and R.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: These are an open-source collection of routines (in MATLAB, Python, and R)
statements.note: The three implementation languages and open-source status are stated.

statements.text: The routines can project a selected microenvironmental factor, such as drug or oxygen distribution, onto the clonal traces.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with an option to include a projection of a selected microenvironmental factor, such as the drug or oxygen distribution within the tumor
statements.note: This projection option is described as part of the package.

statements.text: LinG3D was demonstrated on simulated tumours only and was never applied to experimental data.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The utility of LinG3D has been demonstrated through examples of simulated tumors with different number of clones and, additionally, in experimental colony growth assay.
statements.note: It was also demonstrated in an experimental colony growth assay.

statements.text: LinG3D draws lineage graphs faster than existing lineage tree software.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This routine package extends the classical lineage trees, that show cellular clone relationships in time, by adding the space component to show the locations of cellular clones within the 2D tumor tissue patch from computer simulations of tumor evolution models.
statements.note: The comparison with classical lineage trees concerns what is displayed, not speed, which is never measured.

statements.text: HRS-deficient MOC2 tumours showed increased blood vessel and nerve density on immunohistochemistry.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: immunohistochemical analyses of MOC2 tumors revealed reduced blood vessel and nerve density in HRS-deficient tumors
statements.note: Vessel and nerve density were reduced, not increased, in HRS-deficient tumours.

statements.text: Deleting HRS in MOC2 cells cut small extracellular vesicle formation in vitro and reduced tumour growth and metastasis in vivo.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Loss of the exosome/SEV biogenesis protein HRS in MOC2 HNSCC cells impaired SEV formation in vitro and tumor growth and metastasis in vivo.
statements.note: Both the in vitro and in vivo consequences of HRS loss are reported.

statements.text: A drug blocking HRS reduced metastasis in the orthotopic mouse oral carcinoma model.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Further, we employed an immune-competent orthotopic mouse oral carcinoma (MOC) model to investigate how exosome biogenesis affects HNSCC metastasis.
statements.note: Exosome biogenesis was manipulated by genetic loss of HRS; no inhibitor was tested.

statements.text: Candidate cargo proteins measured in circulating EVs of HPV-negative patients correlated significantly with metastatic status.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Analysis of candidate biomarker SEV cargoes in the circulating EVs from HPV-negative HNSCC patients revealed significant correlations of these proteins with metastatic status.
statements.note: This patient-level correlation with metastatic status is reported directly.

statements.text: DFT1 cells escaped ERBB inhibition quickly, without major copy number alterations or significant phosphorylation changes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: DFT1 cells rapidly evading ERBB inhibition without major copy number alterations or significant changes in phosphorylation
statements.note: This is how DFT1 resistance is described in the abstract.

statements.text: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors shrank facial tumours in wild Tasmanian devils.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Two transmissible cancers, Devil Facial Tumour 1 (DFT1) and Devil Facial Tumour 2 (DFT2), have caused a significant decline in the Tasmanian devil population.
statements.note: All drug responses reported come from cell lines; no animals were treated.

statements.text: Imatinib resistance in DFT2 cells came with copy number alterations, ERBB and JAK/STAT activation, and MHCI downregulation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: DFT2 cell resistance is accompanied by copy number alterations and an activation of ERBB and JAK/STAT signalling with MHCI downregulation
statements.note: These are exactly the features accompanying DFT2 resistance.

statements.text: Targeting ERBB and PDGFR together was antagonistic in DFT1 cells.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Dual targeting of ERBB and PDGFR shows synergistic effects in DFT1 and may prevent resistance emergence.
statements.note: Dual targeting is reported as synergistic, the opposite of antagonistic.

statements.text: Clustered transposon insertions raised the rate of chromosomal rearrangements in the model.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We conclude that 1) dense chromatin packing that hinders transposase access as well as 2) a local loss of compaction upon transposon insertion favor clustered transposon insertion via loop formation.
statements.note: The model addresses where insertions land, not any downstream rearrangement.

statements.text: Alu sequences were more flexible than the genome average, most LINE-1 sequences less flexible, and young elements the most flexible.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Both Alu and LINE-1 deviate in their sequence-inherent flexibility from the overall genome, with above-average flexibility for Alu and below-average flexibility for most LINE-1 sequences. Flexibility was highest in young transposons
statements.note: These flexibility comparisons are reported directly.

statements.text: Alu clustering correlated with reduced chromatin accessibility.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: For Alu elements, this clustering correlates with increased chromatin accessibility.
statements.note: The correlation reported is with increased, not reduced, accessibility.

statements.text: Human cell line repeat data showed extensive clustering of both heterochromatic LINE-1 and euchromatic Alu elements.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Our analysis of human cell line genomic repeat data reveals extensive clustering of heterochromatic LINE-1 elements and euchromatic Alu elements.
statements.note: Extensive clustering of both families is the reported bioinformatic finding.

statements.text: Fifty of the selected serum samples were used to purify circulating exovesicles and cell-free DNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Of the total number of samples selected, 50 were used to isolate and purify exovesicles from circulating serum and cell-free DNA (cfDNA).
statements.note: The abstract states that 50 samples went into the exovesicle and cfDNA purification.

statements.text: Cell-free DNA amplified with SAT primers was positive in only a minority of the samples tested.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: However, isolation of cfDNA for T. cruzi and amplification with SAT primers also showed 100% positivity.
statements.note: cfDNA with SAT primers gave 100% positivity, not a minority.

statements.text: Nested PCR detected the parasite in more patients than serological testing did.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Parasite detection in chronically ill patients is restricted to serological tests that only determine previous contact and not the presence of the parasite, especially in those patients undergoing treatment evaluation or in newborns.
statements.note: Serology defined the cohort rather than being compared head-to-head with PCR for detection rate.

statements.text: Amplification with the kDNA primers 121F-122R gave 100% positivity, while SAT primers gave 96%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a percentage positivity of 100% was obtained for all positive samples assayed with the kDNA-specific primers and 96% when SAT primers were used
statements.note: These are the two positivity rates reported for the purified nucleic acids.

statements.text: In the 220 kb interferon-alpha domain, 77 of 175 transposable elements were young L1 copies from 36 subfamilies.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 77 of its 175 TEs are evolutionary young L1 copies from 36 subfamilies
statements.note: These counts for the interferon-alpha domain are stated exactly.

statements.text: Those young L1 copies had a mean divergence of 135.7, against 188.2 genome-wide.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: at mean divergence 135.7 against 188.2 genome-wide
statements.note: The abstract gives both divergence values, local and genome-wide.

statements.text: Transposable elements in the interferon-alpha domain raise interferon-alpha gene expression.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: This is consistent with recent L1 activity and could indicate a recent evolutionary arms-race affecting innate immune gene regulation.
statements.note: The map is positional and offered as a baseline; no gene expression was measured.

statements.text: Alu elements were enriched near genes for lipid metabolism and olfactory perception.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Alu elements were linked to RNA processing and splicing; MIR elements were associated with zinc homeostasis and voltage-gated potassium channel genes; LINE elements were enriched near genes related to lipid metabolism and olfactory perception
statements.note: Alu elements were linked to RNA processing and splicing; lipid metabolism and olfaction were the LINE associations.

statements.text: Patients with high RNF213 expression did significantly worse on combined anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 therapy.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: patients with high RNF213 expression experienced significant survival advantages when receiving combined anti-PD-1 and anti-CTLA-4 immunotherapies
statements.note: High RNF213 expression went with significant survival advantages on that combination.

statements.text: RNF213 was overexpressed in glioblastoma and endometrial carcinoma and underexpressed in lung and prostate adenocarcinoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: RNF213 demonstrated variable expression levels across different cancer types, with notable overexpression observed in glioblastoma and endometrial carcinoma, while underexpression was detected in lung adenocarcinoma and prostate adenocarcinoma.
statements.note: These are the four tumour types named for over- and underexpression.

statements.text: High RNF213 expression meant worse survival in acute myeloid leukemia and low-grade glioma but better survival in sarcoma and cutaneous melanoma.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Elevated RNF213 expression was linked to unfavorable survival outcomes in acute myeloid leukemia and low-grade glioma, whereas it was associated with better survival in sarcoma and skin cutaneous melanoma.
statements.note: The abstract reports this opposite prognostic direction across the four cancers.

statements.text: RNF213 mutations were more frequent in glioblastoma than in other cancer types.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we performed a systematic analysis of RNF213 expression patterns, mutation frequencies, and their relationships with clinical outcomes
statements.note: Mutation frequencies were analysed, but no per-cancer mutation result is given in the abstract.

statements.text: Promoter methylation explained the lower ASPHD1 expression in high-grade glioma.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Co-expressed gene enrichment and DNA-methylation analyses were performed, and associations between ASPHD1 expression and overall survival (OS) were evaluated.
statements.note: Methylation was analysed, but no methylation result linking it to ASPHD1 expression is reported.

statements.text: Higher ASPHD1 expression went with shorter overall survival in uveal melanoma and mesothelioma.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Pan-cancer analysis further revealed that higher ASPHD1 expression was associated with longer OS in skin cutaneous melanoma (SKCM), uveal melanoma (UVM), and mesothelioma (MESO).
statements.note: Higher ASPHD1 was associated with longer, not shorter, survival in both.

statements.text: ASPHD1 expression fell as WHO grade rose, and low ASPHD1 was an independent adverse prognostic factor.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ASPHD1 expression showed a pronounced inverse correlation with WHO grade, and higher ASPHD1 expression was associated with prolonged OS; multivariable Cox models identified low ASPHD1 as an independent adverse prognostic factor.
statements.note: Both the grade correlation and the multivariable result are reported.

statements.text: ASPHD1 overexpression suppressed glioma cell proliferation, migration and invasion and slowed growth of U87 subcutaneous xenografts.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In glioma cell lines, ASPHD1 overexpression suppressed proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro, and inhibited tumor growth in a subcutaneous U87 xenograft model.
statements.note: These in vitro and xenograft effects of overexpression are reported directly.

statements.text: Patients whose cfDNA rose by week six had median overall survival of 8.35 months against 20.0 months for those whose cfDNA fell.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Patients presenting cfDNA increase at t2 had shorter progression-free survival (PFS; 2.05 vs . 6.1 months, P=0.04) and overall survival (OS; 8.35 vs . 20.0 months, P=0.004) than those with decreased cfDNA.
statements.note: These are the reported median survival times by cfDNA direction at the six-week time point.

statements.text: Somatic mutations in genes including TP53, EGFR and KRAS were found in 58.14% of patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Somatic mutations were found in 58.14% of patients in TP53 , EGFR , KRAS , ALK , PI3KCA and MAP2K1 genes.
statements.note: This mutation-positive fraction and gene list are stated exactly.

statements.text: Patients with over 50% ctDNA decrease or clearance early in treatment had a 3.34 times higher risk of progression.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Patients with >50% decrease or clearance in ctDNA from baseline to early treatment had 3.34 times lower risk for progression and improved survival outcomes (P=0.03).
statements.note: The reported risk was 3.34 times lower, not higher.

statements.text: PD-L1 expression on circulating tumour cells predicted progression-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: CTCs were detected in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and characterised according to programme death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) and Ki67.
statements.note: PD-L1 was measured on CTCs, but only the Ki67 index is tied to outcome in the abstract.

statements.text: Of 54 public tick genome assemblies, 34 from 21 species were judged suitable for downstream analyses.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: From the 54 tick assemblies, we identify 34 high-quality assemblies from 21 species that are suitable for downstream analyses.
statements.note: These assembly and species counts are stated exactly.

statements.text: Assemblies built from pooled individuals carried more contamination than those from single ticks.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Then we evaluate the impact of biological source material and sequencing platforms on these tick genome assemblies.
statements.note: Source material was evaluated, but the abstract gives no result for pooled versus single individuals.

statements.text: Around half of the roughly 1,000 tick species already have a genome assembly.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Ticks are blood-feeding arthropods with approximately 1,000 species, however, only 24 species currently have a genome assembly.
statements.note: Only 24 of about 1,000 species have an assembly.

statements.text: Hard tick genomes average 2.4 Gbp, and transposable elements make up at least 68% of Ixodes assemblies.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: large genome size (on average 2.4 Gbp for hard ticks), and abundant transposable elements (at least 68% of the assembly for Ixodes species)
statements.note: Both figures are given among the reasons tick assemblies are difficult.

statements.text: End motif deconvolution showed DNASE1L3 activity increasing thirty minutes after the meal.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Deconvolutional analysis of cfDNA end motifs showed that DNASE1L3 activity decreased at the 30-minute postprandial state, while DNASE1 and DFFB activities increased at the 2-hour postprandial state.
statements.note: DNASE1L3 activity decreased at 30 minutes; it was DNASE1 and DFFB that rose, and at two hours.

statements.text: Thirty minutes after eating, 70-150 bp cfDNA fragments increased and 151-250 bp fragments decreased, reversing two hours later.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we observed a significant increase in short cfDNA fragments (70-150 bp) and a decrease in long fragments (151-250 bp) at the 30-minute postprandial state, followed by an inverse trend two hours later
statements.note: This size shift and its reversal are the reported fragmentomic result.

statements.text: What the participants ate determined the size of the postprandial shift in cfDNA fragmentation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We assessed the effect of postprandial states on cfDNA fragment size distribution and utilized deconvolutional analysis of end motifs to determine the potential roles of DNA nucleases in cfDNA fragmentation.
statements.note: Only fasting versus postprandial timing was compared; meal composition is never considered.

statements.text: The study sequenced 30 plasma samples from 10 healthy individuals at fasting and two postprandial time points.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We performed shallow whole-genome sequencing of 30 plasma samples from 10 healthy individuals at fasting and postprandial (30-min and 2-h time points).
statements.note: These sample counts and time points are stated in the methods.

statements.text: Parietal lobe tumours were resected less completely than frontal lobe tumours.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Tumor locations were determined using our in-house tool, "tumorVQ", followed by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis based on tumor position.
statements.note: Survival was compared by tumour position only; extent of surgical resection is never reported.

statements.text: Pre-operative MRI scans and genomic data from 123 glioblastoma patients in TCIA and TCGA were analysed.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We analysed pre-operative MRI scans and genomic data from 123 GBM patients (TCIA and TCGA).
statements.note: This is the cohort size and data type stated in the methods.

statements.text: Parietal lobe glioblastomas had worse survival than tumours in other lobes, most markedly against frontal lobe tumours.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Kaplan-Meier analysis showed worse survival for tumors in the parietal lobe compared to other lobes, especially frontal lobe tumors.
statements.note: This is the survival pattern the Kaplan-Meier analysis produced.

statements.text: Higher GLDM DependanceEntropy (LLL) and lower FirstOrder Mean (HLL) were the radiomic features linked to increased risk.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Radiomic features, lower GLDM DependanceEntropy (LLL) and higher FirstOrder Mean (HLL), were strongly linked to increase risk.
statements.note: The directions are swapped: lower DependanceEntropy and higher FirstOrder Mean carried the risk.

statements.text: ctDNA was detectable in 45.8% of patients before neoadjuvant chemotherapy and fell to 8.7% afterwards.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA was detected in 45.8% of patients before neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Detection was similar by T-stage ( P = .18). The rate of detectable ctDNA significantly decreased after chemotherapy (and pre-TES) to 8.7%
statements.note: Both detection rates, before and after chemotherapy, are reported.

statements.text: ctDNA detection before chemotherapy differed significantly between T-stages.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Detection was similar by T-stage ( P = .18).
statements.note: Detection was similar across T-stages, with a non-significant P value.

statements.text: Total mesorectal excision was recommended for all four patients with detectable ctDNA against 16 of 42 patients with undetectable ctDNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with recommended TME for 100% (n = 4 of 4) of patients with ctDNA detected versus 38.1% (n = 16 of 42) of patients with undetectable ctDNA
statements.note: These are the reported proportions recommended for surgery by ctDNA status.

statements.text: ctDNA status after chemotherapy predicted overall survival in the trial patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: ctDNA testing identified cancers with inadequate response to chemotherapy in patients for whom TME was recommended.
statements.note: ctDNA is tied to the surgical recommendation and recurrence counts, with no survival analysis reported.

statements.text: Loss of RRsS1 reduced 24-nt siRNA accumulation at a subset of CLSY3/4-dependent loci, especially those with high Pol IV enrichment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Loss of RRsS1 significantly impairs 24-nt siRNA accumulation at a subset of CLSY3/4-dependent loci, particularly those exhibiting high Pol IV enrichment.
statements.note: This is the siRNA phenotype reported for loss of RRsS1.

statements.text: Plants lacking RRsS1 show transposon mobilisation in reproductive tissues.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Cytosine DNA methylation established by RNA-directed DNA methylation (RdDM) is critical for transposon silencing and genome integrity in plants.
statements.note: Transposon silencing is given as the pathway's background role; no transposon activity was measured in the mutant.

statements.text: GDE1 and CLSY3/4 are not needed for RRsS1 to associate with chromatin.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: We show that chromatin association of RRsS1 is stabilized by GDE1 and CLSY3/4.
statements.note: The abstract reports that these factors stabilize RRsS1 on chromatin.

statements.text: RRsS1 is a chimeric protein built from HRDC, Nudix and DRBM modules.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: characterize RRsS1 as a chimeric protein containing HRDC, Nudix, and DRBM modules
statements.note: Structural modelling and biochemical assays characterised exactly this domain composition.

statements.text: The integrative and conjugative element that was detected carried several of the resistance genes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Although an ICE was detected, no resistance genes linked to this element were found.
statements.note: An ICE was found, but no resistance genes were linked to it.

statements.text: Across the genomes analysed, 20 antimicrobial resistance genes were identified, with Ermx the most predominant.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Bioinformatic analyses identified 20 antimicrobial resistance genes in this species, with the Ermx gene being the most predominant.
statements.note: This gene count and the predominance of Ermx are stated exactly.

statements.text: Ermx confers resistance to macrolide antibiotics in Corynebacterium striatum.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Bioinformatic analyses identified 20 antimicrobial resistance genes in this species, with the Ermx gene being the most predominant.
statements.note: Ermx is named as the most frequent resistance gene, but the abstract never says which antimicrobials it acts against.

statements.text: Resistance genes were mainly found in plasmid sequence regions and class 1 integrons.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Resistance genes were mainly associated with plasmid sequence regions and class 1 integrons.
statements.note: This is where the resistance genes were predominantly located.
